outcome: Prevalence of LUTS (urinary incontinence, increased daytime frequency, nocturia, and urgency) at late pregnancy, 6-8 weeks postpartum, and 1 year postpartum
Risk factors for LUTS one year postpartum
cohort: 1243 pregnant women consecutively enrolled during pregnancy in the obstetrical wards of a tertiary hospital
finding: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are highly prevalent during pregnancy and the postnatal period, with age, occupation, gestational diabetes mellitus, history of urinary tract infection, history of LUTS, age at first birth, and mode of delivery being significant risk factors for LUTS one year postpartum.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with a higher prevalence of LUTS postpartum.
